title: Discovery: High-throughput embedding sharding & hybrid routing (BlueOak Analytics)
summary: Initial discovery for a high-throughput retrieval+rerank pilot. BlueOak wants to evaluate Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private for production embeddings + hybrid reranking. Key concerns: shard strategy for vector DB, embedding dimensionality, throughput (embeds/sec and topK rerank latency), cost vs tail-latency tradeoffs, VPC connectivity and audit logs. Agreed next steps: share benchmark template, Redwood to propose pilot config (dedicated pool sizing + routing rules), customer to provide sample workload and target SLOs.

deployment modes: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-28
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Maya (BlueOak Head of Search), Omar (Platform), Priya (ML Eng)

Auto summary (auto-gen): BlueOak exploring Redwood for embedding generation, vector DB integration and a two-stage retrieval+rerank pilot. Talked through sharding strategies, embedding dims, throughput needs and private vs dedicated deployment tradeoffs.

[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, hmm, can you hear me okay?
[00:03] Maya (BlueOak): yep, loud and clear, thanks.
[00:06] Samir: great. quick intros on our side: im samir, account lead at Redwood, and lena is our solutions engineer who will jump into the infra and perf details.
[00:15] Lena (Redwood SE): hi all, excited to dig in.
[00:18] Maya: im maya, i run search at blueoak, we handle analytics for retail and we're looking to improve relevance with embeddings + rerank.
[00:25] Omar: hey, omar, platform eng, i'll be owner for infra and networking.
[00:29] Priya: priya, ml engineer, i'll own the embed pipeline and evaluation.

[02:00] Samir: cool, top-level, are you leaning hosted, dedicated, or private? what triggered this now?
[02:07] Maya: we saw latency and cost issues with our current setup, and our vendor, um, had some outages, so we want control. Ideally we want a path that starts hosted to move quick, then dedicated or private for production, depending on SLAs.
[02:25] Lena: that's pretty common; for pilot we often run hosted to get baselines then propose dedicated pools that match throughput. quick question: what's your target qps and tail latency for user-facing search?

[03:10] Priya: for discovery queries we average 800 qps, peak maybe 3.5k qps, and 95th latency target for full retrieval+rerank is under 250 ms. Rerank only (top-50 -> cross-encoder) should be <120 ms ideally.
[03:28] Lena: okay that helps. is your current index an ANN store like pinecone or self-hosted faiss?
[03:34] Maya: we're on a hybrid: a sharded Milvus cluster for production, but for experiments we're on pinecone. we plan to keep Milvus on-prem for GDPR reasons for some europe data.

[05:00] Omar: network question — if we run private, do we need to open persistent tunnels or is it VPC peering? also what about audit logs and KMS?
[05:12] Samir: good q. for private we support VPC peering and private endpoints, and keys can be KMS-backed; we also provide audit logs and retention options. i'll send the SOC2 and admin docs after.
[05:25] Maya: perfect.

[06:10] Lena: back to architecture — the common pattern we recommend is two-stage: ANN to retrieve top-K (we typically do K=100) then a lightweight embed-sim or cross-encoder rerank for top-10. For throughput you can push most cost into ANN and keep reranker scale low.
[06:35] Priya: for us top-K 100 sounds right. question: our current embeddings are 1536 dims using a proprietary embedder — could we get similar recall with smaller dims? 512 or 768?
[06:50] Lena: tradeoff is recall vs vector storage and ANN speed. 1536 often yields better recall for wide corpora, but 768 can be near parity on curated datasets; it depends on your embedding model and downstream reranker. for cost we show using 768 reduces storage ~2x and embed generation cost as well.

[08:00] Samir: to add, we can run A/B in pilot: generate both 1536 and 768 and run offline eval on your query set to compare recall/ndcg. lena, we can put a recommended quantization profile — e.g., 8bit quant for cheaper embeddings in storage — but be careful, quant can slightly affect nearest neighbors.
[08:22] Lena: yes and also the vector DB's index type matters — HNSW vs IVF vs PQ — some combos are better with quantized vectors.

[10:00] Maya: sharding: our Milvus team prefers sharding by customer tenant then date. our docs are 10M rows and growing; expected growth 20% qtr. we worry about tail latency if a shard hot-keys.
[10:18] Lena: for 10M, sharding across nodes with replication helps. Redwood's routing can do region-based fallback too; you can route queries to dedicated pool vs hosted fallback if capacity spikes. we also recommend sub-sharding your vector DB and using fanout limits to keep tail latency bounded.
[10:40] Omar: fanout? you mean how many partitions we query in parallel?
[10:44] Lena: exactly — limiting fanout reduces variability; you can pre-merge hot partitions or use a routing table to send top-candidate partitions only.

[12:30] Priya: on embedding generation throughput — we need to re-embed millions of docs weekly. can Redwood handle bulk embed jobs? what's the expected throughput on Dedicated 4xA100 or similar?
[12:45] Lena: bulk pipelines are common. on dedicated with batching tuned you can hit ~= 3000-6000 embeds per GPU per second depending on model and batch size. with 4xA100 you'd expect tens of thousands per second aggregate for generation if parallelized and network isn't the bottleneck. for hosted we also provide bulk job APIs but with queuing.
[13:10] Samir: important to profile your average doc length; tokens per doc matter a lot for embed throughput. shorter docs = much higher throughput.

[15:00] Maya: re rerank cost: if we cross-encode top50 per query at 800 qps continuously that's expensive. any suggestions to reduce cost?
[15:12] Lena: couple approaches: 1) use a lightweight dot-prod reranker for most queries and only trigger cross-encoder for ambiguous ones; 2) reduce K using a better ANN recall by tuning index and dims; 3) cache rerank results for repeated popular queries. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and caching profiles to reduce unit cost.
[15:35] Priya: the ambiguous triggers could be threshold-based on vector similarity score.

[17:00] Samir: curious — do you need on-prem because of data residency, or is VPC sufficient?
[17:05] Maya: EU data needs to stay in EU region and some PII must not leave our VPC; so VPC/private is likely required for those datasets.
[17:18] Omar: and we need KMS integration with our corporate key.
[17:22] Samir: we support bringing your own KMS for private; we'll share the integration doc.

[19:30] Lena: pod sizing: given your peak 3.5k qps, if you plan to rerank top-50 for all queries, you need substantial dedicated capacity. but if you use hybrid routing — route lower-tier queries to cheaper model or cached answers — you can reduce required nodes by 30-60%. Redwood routing rules can be tuned by latency budget, cost, or region.

[21:00] Maya: hmm, can you explain hybrid routing more concretely?
[21:05] Lena: sure — example: primary route does ANN + cheap rerank (dot-prod) staying under 120ms. secondary route (for high-SLA customers) uses heavyweight cross-encoder running on dedicated low-latency pool. rules evaluate token budget, user type, or direct API flag. fallback policies can downgrade to cached results during overload.

[23:00] Omar: on the vector DB sync, we have an edge ingestion pipeline that writes vectors to S3 and then pushes to Milvus; we'd like a safe reconciliation job if some writes fail. does Redwood help with reconciliation?
[23:15] Samir: we have tooling and best-practice docs for ingestion and reconciliation; for dedicated/private deployments we can run a connector that watches S3 and reconciles diffs into your VDB. we'll share connector code examples.

[25:00] Priya: evaluation metrics — we'll measure recall@10, ndcg, p95 latency for retrieval and p95 end-to-end. also cost per 1M queries.
[25:12] Samir: perfect — send those KPIs and we'll map pilot objectives accordingly.

[27:30] Maya: security checklist — we need SOC2 attestation, SSO/SAML support, RBAC and per-route audit logs.
[27:40] Samir: we are SOC2 Type II, SSO via SAML/OIDC supported, RBAC in console and per-token audit logs. will attach security whitepaper.

[29:00] Lena: small gotcha — when you do real-time embeddings at high qps, watch out for KV cache semantics; it's mostly for autoregressive workloads but some internal caches can help warm up models. for bulk re-embed jobs caching isnt applicable.
[29:20] Omar: i think we mislabelled KV earlier in our notes, thanks.

[31:00] Priya: do you support live A/B of models where we can serve different dims for sub-populations?
[31:06] Lena: yes, you can pin model versions and route traffic percentage-based; Redwood Console has rollout controls and experiment metrics so you can compare recall and latency between 1536 and 768 models.

[33:30] Maya: what about cold start times for dedicated pools — if traffic spikes will new nodes come up quickly?
[33:40] Samir: autoscaling config is flexible; dedicated pools can have burst capacity reserved for spikes, but warmup time for GPUs varies; we recommend a small buffer for steady state or pre-warm for known events.

[35:10] Lena: ops note — network egress can be a cost vector if your vector DB is in a different cloud region; in private deployments colocating compute and DB reduces egress and latency.

[37:00] Omar: great point. our Milvus is on-prem in eu-west, so we'd prefer Redwood Private in eu-west edge.
[37:08] Samir: we offer region placements and private control plane in eu-west for customers with those needs.

[39:00] Maya: benchmarks — what do you need from us to run a pilot benchmark?
[39:04] Lena: sample query set (50k), doc vectors or subset (100k-1M depending), expected token distribution and peak/avg qps, and your success KPIs (ndcg thresholds, latency SLO). we will run head-to-head with a recommended index and rerank config.

[41:00] Priya: about costs: can you ballpark cost difference hosted vs dedicated for our expected throughput?
[41:08] Samir: rough ballpark: hosted covers baseline dev/testing and small-scale production, but at sustained throughput your per-token cost is typically higher vs dedicated with reserved capacity. dedicated with 4xA100 pool and moderate ingress could be 30-60% cheaper on a per-embed basis, depending on utilization and model size. we'll provide a more precise estimate once we have sample load.

[43:20] Maya: timeline — we want a pilot in April, production in June if results look good.
[43:28] Samir: that timeline sounds doable. next step: i'll share the benchmark sheet and pilot options; lena will propose pool sizes.

[45:00] Omar: any questions about integration? we use CICD for deployments and need terraform examples for infra.
[45:10] Lena: we have terraform modules and helm charts for private/dedicated deployments; we'll include examples in the repo link.

[47:30] Priya: for rerank models, do you host cross-encoders or do we bring our own model?
[47:38] Lena: both — you can bring your own model artifact and we can host it in private with your KMS, or use our curated cross-encoders. hosting your own gives more control and helps with compliance.

[49:00] Maya: curious about monitoring — can we see token-level cost and per-route latency breakdown?
[49:06] Samir: yes, Redwood Console gives token-level cost, per-model and per-route latency breakdowns, traces, and error rates.

[51:00] Priya: gotcha. one last technical — how do you handle vector updates and near-real-time index changes? we need <30s visibility for new items.
[51:10] Lena: with warm indexing pipelines and smaller shards you can reach sub-30s visibility; we recommend streaming ingestion with a small in-memory buffer and periodic index commits tuned to your write rate. we'll help tune Milvus index params.

[53:00] Maya: ok this was super helpful. can you summarize next steps?
[53:10] Samir: sure. recap: we'll send benchmark template and security docs; lena will send pool sizing and a rough cost range; blueoak to share 50k queries + doc subset; schedule pilot kickoff early April.
[53:28] Maya: sounds good.
[54:00] Omar: thanks everyone.
[54:03] Lena: thanks, we'll follow up with links.
[54:10] Samir: end of call, bye.

End transcript.
notes: Customer strongly leaning to VPC/private for EU PII workloads
Pilot timeline: April kickoff, June prod target
Key KPI: p95 end-to-end <250ms, rerank <120ms, ndcg improvement target to be provided by customer
